thread:
maria.support: Elena, we've got a paying customer reporting parse failures in streaming JSON mode. They see their client throw 'Unexpected end of JSON input' around byte 14123. They say it only happens ~3% of streams. Request ID: req-9a8b. Attaching their raw tail.

sam.eng: Can you paste the exact last bytes they received?

elena.customer: here's the raw tail we got (we're using our Node client)
```
...\"choices\":[{\"index\":0,\"message\":{\"content\":\"{\\\"items\\\":[{\\\"id\\\":1,\\\"value\\\":\\\"foo\\\"},{\\\"id\\\":2,\\\"value\\\":\\\"bar\\\"}],\\\"meta\\\":{\\\"cursor\\\":42},\\\"incomplete\\\":true
```
(missing closing brackets and brace)

sam.eng: :eyes: that looks like the stream cut before the final `}]}`. Do you have edge/nginx logs for req-9a8b? Check bytes_sent and whether the connection closed with FIN/RST.

maria.support: Here's proxy log snippet the customer provided:
```
[proxy] 3230000000 req=9a8b bytes_sent=14135 status=200 upstream_status=- code=HUP
```
proxy claims HUP on upstream.

vikram_sre: HUP probably from upstream process closing FD after flush. Could be keepalive timeout on LB causing mid-chunk termination. Also ask customer whether they have an intermediary (CF, Fastly) configured to drop idle connections.

elena.customer: They're behind a corporate proxy chain; they say CPU spike rolled through their outbound proxy. But curl reproduces locally if we run `curl -N --http1.1 <url>` and then kill connection at ~14KB using `sleep 0.3; kill -9 <pid>` — we can reproduce trimmed tail.

sam.eng: Repro is huge — thanks. Two immediate asks:
1) Does our runtime ever send a final chunk without CRLF? 2) Are we flush-chunking partial objects? Need logs from runtime: stream flush events + last bytes emitted for req-9a8b.

repro-bot: Replay created: /replays/3230000000/req-9a8b

maria.support: Runtime log excerpt:
```
[runtime] stream_emit req=9a8b bytes=14140 last_chunk_size=48 status=streaming
[runtime] downstream_closed req=9a8b reason=socket_write_error errno=104
```

vikram_sre: errno=104 is ECONNRESET from peer. That means peer closed — either the customer's proxy or intermediate closed mid-stream. If upstream did send full `}]}` and socket got reset while client already had data, client might still miss last bytes. But logs show last_chunk_size=48 — can we print actual bytes? Also check for chunked transfer encoding and whether trailing CRLF gets included.

sam.eng: Quick mitigation: update SDK to tolerate streams that end mid-object by buffering and attempt to reissue a final small range request to patch missing tail. Also make a server-side defensive measure: include periodic final keepalive heartbeat frame and explicit \"stream_end\" sentinel JSON object to reduce ambiguous final-brace loss.

elena.customer: Customer accepts workaround if we can provide short-term SDK patch. They also want root cause — they run corporate proxy that enforces connection idle=30s. Our stream lasted 2.1s — so not idle. Might be other middlebox.

maria.support: Action items: @sam.eng get runtime byte dumps for req-9a8b; @vikram_sre audit LB/proxy keepalive chain; @elena.customer request pcap from customer or advise them to run `curl -v --no-buffer` to capture remote close flag. We'll loop in infra team if logs show server sent final bytes.

sam.eng: I'll add small debug flag to runtime: emit final-chunk-hex and upstream-flush-callsite for next 24h. Putting a canary patch behind feature flag.

vikram_sre: Also rolling out advisory to SDK teams: treat Unexpected end as recoverable for streaming JSON by attempting transparent tail re-fetch for last 256 bytes when feasible.

elena.customer: :thumbsup: thanks, please keep me posted. Customer is sensitive due to parsing errors in production.

maria.support: Noted — closing loop when we have runtime trace. :phone:
